sanskrit: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते ॥
hindiTranslation: इस संसारमें क्षर नाशवान् और अक्षर अविनाशी  ये दो प्रकारके पुरुष हैं ।  सम्पूर्ण प्राणियोंके शरीर नाशवान् और कूटस्थ जीवात्मा अविनाशी कहा जाता है ॥
englishTranslation: In this world, there are two kinds of beings: the perishable and the imperishable. All embodied beings are perishable; the steadfast one is called imperishable.
essence: What changes is not the whole of you.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: There are two kinds of existence here: what changes and what does not. Bodies pass away, but the unchanging reality within remains.
simpleInsight: You can stop clinging to what fades and rest in what does not.
detailedMeaning: Krishna widens the frame beyond the war: all bodies are temporary, and the steady reality within them lasts. This verse prepares Arjuna to act without mistaking the body for the whole person.
modernRelevance: Standing at an old friend's funeral, you see the body that changed over fifty years. Krishna separates that perishable part from the steady one, which he calls imperishable, and asks you to know both.
translationLiteral: द्वौ (two) / इमौ (these) / पुरुषौ (beings) / लोके (in the world) / क्षरः (perishable) / च (and) / अक्षरः (imperishable) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / क्षरः (perishable) / सर्वाणि (all) / भूतानि (beings) / कूटस्थः (steadfast) / अक्षरः (imperishable) / उच्यते (is called)
insight: Two kinds of purusha exist, Krishna says: the perishable, which is every body, and the steady imperishable.

quoteVariants.text: All embodied beings pass. The steadfast one does not.
Everything changing is not the whole story.
What changes is not all you are.
